chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan — both from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

'Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir used to say: I did not think that Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) would leave behind a successor more virtuous than himself — until I saw his son, Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him). I intended to admonish him, but he admonished me instead.' His companions said to him: 'With what did he admonish you?'

He said: I went out to one of the outskirts of Medina during an intensely hot time. Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali met me — he was a heavyset, large man — leaning upon two black servants, or two freed men. I said to myself: Glory be to God! An elder from the elders of Quraysh, at this hour, in this state, in pursuit of worldly livelihood. I shall surely admonish him!

So I approached him and greeted him. He returned my greeting with a rebuke, while he was dripping with sweat. I said: May God keep you well — an elder from the elders of Quraysh, at this hour, in this state, in pursuit of worldly livelihood. Tell me, if your appointed hour arrived while you were in this state, what would you do?

He said: If death came to me in this state, it would come to me while I was engaged in an act of obedience to God, Mighty and Majestic — by which I protect myself and my family from depending on you and on the people. Rather, what I truly feared was if death came to me while I was engaged in an act of disobedience to God. So I said: You speak the truth — may God have mercy on you. I intended to admonish you, but you have admonished me instead.

key_terms.أكف نفسي وعيالي: I protect myself and my family — the Imam's justification for working; financial self-sufficiency as a moral and religious virtue
key_terms.طاعة الله: Obedience to God — encompassing not just ritual acts but also lawful earning and family provision
key_terms.طلب الدنيا: Pursuit of worldly livelihood — here reinterpreted by the Imam as an act of piety when done to fulfill family obligations and avoid dependence
key_terms.معصية الله: Disobedience to God — what one should truly fear meeting death in, not honest labor

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Baqir teach that working for a livelihood is a form of worship in Islam?
ai.summary: This narrative, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), recounts how Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir — a well-known Sunni ascetic and scholar of Medina — was corrected by Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS). Ibn al-Munkadir, seeing the Imam working outdoors in the summer heat, misjudged the act as worldly indulgence. The Imam's response revealed the Islamic teaching that honest labor to support one's family constitutes an act of worship and obedience to God, and that the real fear should be dying in a state of disobedience, not while engaged in lawful livelihood. This hadith is significant in the chapter on the Imam modeling frugal but dignified self-sufficiency — countering any asceticism that would depend on others.
